clues.text: This city was founded in 1872 on the east bank of a great river, in the middle of the northern plains. It began as a railroad town.
clues.narrowing: Points to a plains city founded on a big river's east bank.

source.quote: Bismarck was founded by European-Americans in 1872 on the east bank of the Missouri River.

clues.text: Winters here are cold, dry, snowy, and windy. Summers are warm, with storms in the spring and summer months.
clues.narrowing: Keeps far-northern plains capitals with cold, windy winters.

source.quote: Bismarck's climate is characterized by cold, somewhat dry, snowy, and windy winters and warm, humid summers.

clues.text: In 1883, this rail town was made the capital of a vast new land. Six years on, it kept the job when that land became a state.
clues.narrowing: Cuts the list to the town made territory capital in 1883 and state capital in 1889.

source.quote: In 1883, Bismarck was designated as the capital of the Dakota Territory in place of Yankton, South Dakota, and in 1889, as the state capital of the new state of North Dakota.

clues.text: The capitol here is a tall tower of 19 floors, the tallest in the state. Folks call it the skyscraper of the flat plains.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital's capitol is a 19-story state-tallest tower.

source.quote: The 19-story Art Deco capitol is the tallest building in the state, at a height of 241.75 feet (73.69 m).

clues.text: North Dakota's governor works in this town. Its lawmakers meet in the tall capitol on the plains.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the governor and lawmakers of North Dakota work in this city.

source.quote: is the capital city of the U.S. state of North Dakota

reveal.blurb: Railroad men renamed this river town in 1873 for a German leader, hoping to lure railroad money. It became the state capital in 1889, and its 19-story capitol still towers over the plains. The building is the capitol, and the city is the capital. Bismarck is the capital of North Dakota.
